subject: Current Affairs
q: The Charter of the United Nations was signed in 1945 at:
explanation: Delegates of 50 countries signed the Charter on 26 June 1945 at the San Francisco Conference.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The United Nations formally came into existence on:
explanation: The Charter entered into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the five major powers and a majority of other signatories; the day is marked as UN Day.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which organisation was the predecessor of the United Nations?
explanation: The League of Nations, created after the First World War, failed to prevent the Second World War and was replaced by the UN.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which major power never joined the League of Nations, although its own President had championed the idea?
explanation: President Woodrow Wilson proposed the League, but the US Senate refused to ratify the Treaty of Versailles, so the USA never became a member.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Atlantic Charter of 1941, which set out principles later reflected in the UN, was issued by:
explanation: US President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill issued the Atlantic Charter in August 1941, outlining their goals for the post-war world.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first detailed proposals for the structure of the United Nations were drafted in 1944 at:
explanation: At the Dumbarton Oaks conference in Washington (1944), the US, UK, USSR and China drafted proposals that became the basis of the UN Charter.

subject: Current Affairs
q: How many principal organs does the UN Charter establish?
explanation: The Charter creates six principal organs: the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice and Secretariat.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which principal organ of the UN suspended its operations in 1994?
explanation: The Trusteeship Council supervised trust territories; it suspended operations once the last of them became independent in 1994.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following is NOT an official language of the United Nations?
explanation: The six official UN languages are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish; German is not among them.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Enforcement action by the Security Council, including sanctions and the use of force, is authorised under which chapter of the UN Charter?
explanation: Chapter VII deals with action with respect to threats to the peace, breaches of the peace and acts of aggression, and allows binding enforcement measures.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Chapter VI of the UN Charter deals with:
explanation: Chapter VI provides for peaceful means such as negotiation, mediation, conciliation and arbitration to settle disputes.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which Article of the UN Charter recognises the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence?
explanation: Article 51 preserves the right of self-defence if an armed attack occurs, until the Security Council takes necessary measures.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Article 2(4) of the UN Charter requires member states to refrain from:
o: Recognising new states without UN approval
The threat or use of force against other states
explanation: Article 2(4) prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state, a cornerstone of modern international law.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Security Council consists of how many members?
explanation: The Council has five permanent members and ten non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Non-permanent members of the Security Council are elected for a term of:
explanation: The General Assembly elects five of the ten non-permanent members each year for two-year terms; they cannot be immediately re-elected.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The number of non-permanent members of the Security Council was raised from six to ten with effect from:
explanation: A Charter amendment adopted in 1963 entered into force in 1965, enlarging the Council from 11 to 15 members.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The power of veto in the UN Security Council is held by:
explanation: Under Article 27, substantive decisions require the concurring votes of the permanent members, so a negative vote by any one of the five blocks a resolution.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The presidency of the UN Security Council rotates among its members:
explanation: The presidency passes monthly among the fifteen members in English alphabetical order of their names.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The "Uniting for Peace" resolution of 1950 allows the General Assembly to act when:
o: The Secretary-General resigns before his term ends
The Security Council fails to act because of disagreement among its permanent members
A member state refuses to pay its dues
The ICJ cannot reach a verdict
explanation: Resolution 377 lets the Assembly consider threats to peace and recommend collective measures if a veto deadlocks the Security Council.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The People's Republic of China replaced the Republic of China (Taiwan) in the United Nations in:
explanation: General Assembly Resolution 2758 of October 1971 recognised the PRC as the only lawful representative of China, including in its permanent Security Council seat.

subject: Current Affairs
q: After the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, its permanent seat in the Security Council passed to:
explanation: The Russian Federation was accepted as the continuator of the USSR and took over its permanent seat and Charter obligations.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Decisions of the UN General Assembly on important questions, such as budget matters and admission of new members, require:
o: A simple majority of all members
The approval of the Security Council only
A two-thirds majority of members present and voting
explanation: Article 18 requires a two-thirds majority for important questions; other decisions need a simple majority, with each member having one vote.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The President of the UN General Assembly is elected for a term of:
explanation: A new President is elected for each annual session, with the post rotating among regional groups.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
explanation: The Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948 in Paris as a common standard of rights for all peoples.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which country was admitted to the United Nations in 2011 as its 193rd member?
explanation: South Sudan became independent from Sudan in July 2011 and was admitted to the UN the same month.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) has how many members?
explanation: ECOSOC has 54 members elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms, as set by Charter amendments.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) is based in:
explanation: ESCAP, one of ECOSOC's five regional commissions and the one covering Pakistan, has its headquarters in Bangkok.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Court of Justice sits at:
explanation: The ICJ, the principal judicial organ of the UN, sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Court of Justice is composed of how many judges?
explanation: Under its Statute the ICJ has 15 judges, no two of whom may be nationals of the same state.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Judges of the International Court of Justice are elected for a term of:
explanation: ICJ judges serve nine-year terms, with one-third of the bench elected every three years.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Judges of the International Court of Justice are elected by:
o: The General Assembly and the Security Council voting separately
explanation: A candidate must obtain an absolute majority in both the General Assembly and the Security Council.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following can be a party to a contentious case before the International Court of Justice?
explanation: Article 34 of the ICJ Statute provides that only states may be parties in cases before the Court; UN organs may only request advisory opinions.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Secretary-General is appointed by:
o: A vote of all member states' heads of government
The General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
explanation: Article 97 provides that the Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council, where the veto applies.

subject: Current Affairs
q: By established practice, the UN Secretary-General serves a term of:
explanation: The Charter does not fix the term, but since 1946 Secretaries-General have been appointed for renewable five-year terms.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first Secretary-General of the United Nations was:
explanation: Trygve Lie of Norway served as the first Secretary-General from 1946 to 1952.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which UN Secretary-General died in an air crash in 1961 while on a peace mission related to the Congo crisis?
explanation: Dag Hammarskjöld of Sweden was killed when his plane crashed in Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia) in September 1961.

subject: Current Affairs
q: U Thant, the third Secretary-General of the UN, was a national of:
explanation: U Thant of Burma served from 1961 to 1971 and was the first Asian to hold the office.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first Secretary-General of the UN from the Arab world and Africa was:
explanation: Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt served from 1992 to 1996.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which UN Secretary-General shared the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize with the United Nations itself?
explanation: The 2001 prize was awarded jointly to the UN and Kofi Annan for their work for a better organised and more peaceful world.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first UN Secretary-General from Latin America was:
explanation: Javier Pérez de Cuéllar of Peru served two terms from 1982 to 1991.

subject: Current Affairs
q: António Guterres, who became UN Secretary-General in January 2017, had earlier served as Prime Minister of:
explanation: Guterres was Prime Minister of Portugal (1995–2002) and later UN High Commissioner for Refugees before becoming Secretary-General.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Ban Ki-moon, UN Secretary-General from 2007 to 2016, belonged to:
explanation: Ban Ki-moon was South Korea's foreign minister before serving two terms as the eighth Secretary-General.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The main European headquarters of the United Nations is located in:
explanation: The UN Office at Geneva, housed in the Palais des Nations, is the largest UN duty station after New York.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The headquarters of UNESCO is in:
explanation: UNESCO, the UN agency for education, science and culture, is headquartered in Paris.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is headquartered in:
explanation: FAO, which leads international efforts against hunger, has its headquarters in Rome.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) has its headquarters in:
explanation: IFAD, which finances rural development in poor countries, is one of three UN food agencies based in Rome.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Food Programme, the UN's main food-assistance agency, is based in:
explanation: WFP is headquartered in Rome alongside FAO and IFAD.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Health Organization is headquartered in:
explanation: WHO, the UN specialised agency for international public health, has its headquarters in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Labour Organization has its headquarters in:
explanation: The ILO, which sets international labour standards, is based in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Universal Postal Union is headquartered in:
explanation: The UPU, founded in 1874, coordinates international postal services from Bern, Switzerland.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is headquartered in:
explanation: The ITU, the UN agency for information and communication technologies, is based in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Meteorological Organization is based in:
explanation: The WMO coordinates global weather, climate and water observation from its Geneva headquarters.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) has its headquarters in:
explanation: WIPO, which administers international treaties on patents, trademarks and copyright, is based in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is headquartered in:
explanation: ICAO, created by the 1944 Chicago Convention, sets global civil aviation standards from Montreal, Canada.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is headquartered in:
explanation: The IMO, responsible for shipping safety and preventing marine pollution by ships, is the only UN agency based in the United Kingdom.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Atomic Energy Agency has its headquarters in:
explanation: The IAEA, which promotes peaceful nuclear energy and verifies safeguards, is based at the Vienna International Centre.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) is headquartered in:
explanation: UNIDO, which promotes industrial development in developing countries, is based in Vienna.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is headquartered in:
explanation: UNEP, set up in 1972, is based in Nairobi, making it one of the few UN bodies headquartered in the Global South.

subject: Current Affairs
q: UN-Habitat, the UN programme for human settlements and sustainable urban development, is based in:
explanation: UN-Habitat has its headquarters in Nairobi, alongside UNEP.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), established in 1964, is based in:
explanation: UNCTAD, set up to address the trade and development concerns of developing countries, has its secretariat in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which pair of UN bodies is headquartered in New York?
explanation: UNICEF and UNDP are based in New York; UNHCR and WHO are in Geneva, FAO and WFP in Rome, and UNEP and UN-Habitat in Nairobi.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is headquartered in:
explanation: UNHCR, established in 1950, is based in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which UN specialised agency is the oldest, having been founded in 1865?
explanation: The ITU began as the International Telegraph Union in 1865; the UPU dates from 1874 and the ILO from 1919.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Labour Organization was created in 1919 as part of:
o: The Covenant of the United Nations
explanation: The ILO was established by Part XIII of the Treaty of Versailles and became the first specialised agency of the UN in 1946.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The ILO is unique among UN agencies because its governing bodies bring together representatives of:
explanation: The ILO's tripartite structure gives workers' and employers' delegates an equal voice with governments in setting labour standards.

subject: Current Affairs
q: UNICEF was originally created in 1946 to provide emergency relief to:
o: Refugees from the partition of India
Children affected by the Second World War
explanation: The UN International Children's Emergency Fund was set up to help children in war-ravaged Europe and China; its mandate later became permanent and global.

subject: Current Affairs
q: UNRWA provides education, health and relief services specifically to:
explanation: The UN Relief and Works Agency was established in 1949 to assist refugees displaced by the 1948 Arab–Israeli war and their descendants.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The main task of UNHCR is to:
explanation: The UN Refugee Agency leads international action to protect refugees, forcibly displaced people and stateless persons.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which UN agency deals mainly with population issues and reproductive health?
explanation: The United Nations Population Fund works on reproductive health, family planning and population data.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which UN body leads international efforts against illicit drugs and transnational organised crime?
explanation: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime, based in Vienna, supports states against drug trafficking, organised crime, corruption and terrorism.

subject: Current Affairs
q: World Heritage Sites are inscribed on the World Heritage List by:
explanation: UNESCO administers the 1972 World Heritage Convention, under which sites of outstanding universal value are listed.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Human Rights Council replaced the Commission on Human Rights in:
explanation: The General Assembly created the Human Rights Council in 2006 to replace the widely criticised Commission on Human Rights.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Human Rights Council is composed of how many member states?
explanation: The Council's 47 members are elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms on the basis of equitable geographical distribution.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Universal Periodic Review, under which the human rights record of every UN member state is examined, is conducted by:
explanation: Since 2008 the Human Rights Council has reviewed the human rights situation of all UN member states in successive cycles.

subject: Current Affairs
q: UN Women, the UN entity for gender equality and the empowerment of women, was established in:
explanation: The General Assembly created UN Women in 2010 by merging four existing UN bodies working on women's issues.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN Peacebuilding Commission, which helps countries emerging from conflict, was established in:
explanation: The General Assembly and Security Council jointly created the Peacebuilding Commission in December 2005 following the World Summit.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first armed UN peacekeeping force, UNEF, was deployed in 1956 in response to:
explanation: The first UN Emergency Force was sent to supervise the withdrawal of British, French and Israeli forces from Egyptian territory after the Suez Crisis.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Health Organization came into being in:
explanation: The WHO Constitution entered into force on 7 April 1948, a date now marked as World Health Day.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Atomic Energy Agency was established in:
explanation: The IAEA was set up in 1957, inspired by President Eisenhower's "Atoms for Peace" proposal of 1953.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The "Atoms for Peace" proposal that led to the creation of the IAEA was made in 1953 by:
explanation: President Eisenhower proposed Atoms for Peace in a speech to the UN General Assembly in December 1953.
